findings: HEADLINE, new and root-caused: the picture still stacks one word per line on every template caption run, and the cause is not the fitter. caption.py write_ass computes a single `margin = round(args.margin * scale)` and writes it into MarginL, MarginR and MarginV of the Style row. args.margin is the platform's VERTICAL safe margin in ASS units (tiktok 63, shorts 52); scaled by play_h/288 that is 420 px, so at PlayResX 1080 the emitted Style is `...,2,420,420,420,1` and the text column is 1080 - 420 - 420 = 240 px. libass then wraps every word. The Opus grader reproduced it from scratch on a fresh 1080x1920 clip and got 'Hello' over 'world'.

The bug is confined to the generated-ASS path - --animate/--karaoke - which is exactly the path every delivery template takes (render.py passes --animate pop --karaoke --margin 63/52). The plain SRT path burns force_style with MarginV only and is correctly typeset. cs2, the one caption run in this set that drove caption.py by hand with --platform shorts and no animation, is the only run whose lines run the full frame width - the eval data corroborates the diagnosis on its own.

This is why the fit stats and the sheets disagree. The fitter budgets play_w * 0.9 (972 px) while libass lays out into 240 px, so `split: 0` and `text_unchanged: true` are true statements about the ASS text and false statements about the picture. Shrinking cannot rescue it: dl4 reaches the 13-unit floor and still stacks. Today's caption stats in every template report are a measurement of the wrong frame.

The defect has been present since 1.14 introduced --platform margins, and it explains eval 17's and eval 18's 'one word per line' complaints, which were attributed first to the phrase breaker (1.16.1) and then to the unreachable size fitter (1.17.1). Two patches have now been aimed at symptoms of this line. 1.17.2 is the patch that reaches it.

1.17.1's own headline fix is real and stable, and worth saying plainly: fit-size fires on the template path in 12/12 caption runs across three repeats, with identical stats per id and byte-identical output media between reps. What changed since eval 18 is the numbers in the report. The picture is unchanged.

Repeat stability is high everywhere except Look. Across cw1/dl1/dl4/cs1 x3: routing 12/12, honesty 11/12, language and format 12/12, quality spread <= 1 point per id. Whether the agent tells the user about the stacked words is a coin flip - disclosed in 6 of 12, papered over in 5. dl1 disclosed it in reps 1 and 2 but not 3; dl4 never disclosed it in any rep; cw1 disclosed it in all three. A defect that only half the runs report is a defect the eval would have missed at one repeat.

Look-reading is the weakest graded axis at 20/26, and the failure is specific rather than general: five runs describe a contact sheet they produced and opened, and call captions 'legible, inside the lower safe area' while the sheet shows one word per line. The sixth, rc1, wrote a sheet and then said 'pixels not inspected; agent has no image view'. Agents can see the sheet; what they lack is a measurement to check the sentence against.

cs3 rewrote the user's caption text instead of refusing for the third iteration running (3/3). The prompt exists to forbid exactly this, the run disclosed the rewrite, and it still reported Done. SKILL.md gained a caption routing table in 1.17.1 but no refusal line: 'never rewrite, shorten or paraphrase the user's caption text; offer --max-lines or a smaller --min-size instead' needs to be where the agent reads it on this path.

silence.py --filler removes silence gaps by default. fw1 went 12.00 s -> 6.77 s for 'take the filler words out' and fw3 the same; both runs disclosed it in Notes, so the reports are honest, but ~5 s of unasked-for cutting is a surprising default for that request. This is a design question for 1.18, not a defect: either --filler leaves silences alone unless asked, or the SKILL.md row says what it does.

rc1's --cache miss is half a fixture bug. The staged project.json has clips and export only, so the prompt's 'don't redo the captions' names a stage that does not exist, and the agent said so. --cache was still the route, and the run is graded a miss, but as staged rc1 cannot distinguish a cache miss from a correct refusal to care. rc2 is the opposite failure: it reasoned correctly from --help that the cache key includes the ffmpeg version and then rendered nothing at all, where the prompt wanted a real run reporting every stage as a miss.

The counter-example is dl1 (+18%, and dearer still in both repeats), where the spend is the agent looking at a stacked caption it cannot fix. All 26 runs mean 83,796; repeats are consistently dearer than rep1.

follow_ups: 1.17.2 blocker: caption.py write_ass must derive MarginL and MarginR from the platform's horizontal safe fractions * play_w (default the 5% title-safe), independently of MarginV. Regression test asserting Style MarginL + MarginR <= (1 - SAFE_WIDTH_FRACTION) * play_w at tiktok geometry, and an e2e asserting the generated ASS for 'Hello world' at --platform tiktok contains no \N.

1.17.2 blocker: make the fitter (line_em_for_size) measure against the same horizontal budget the Style row will actually grant, so `split: 0`, `size_used` and `text_unchanged` describe the picture. Until they do, every template caption report states numbers the agent cannot falsify.

1.17.2: an explicit refusal line in SKILL.md's caption section - never rewrite, shorten or paraphrase the user's caption text; offer --max-lines or a smaller size instead. cs3 is 3/3 misses across iterations 17, 18 and 19 and prose elsewhere in the file has not closed it.

Give the agent something to check a Look line against: a caption.py --fit-report (or the same numbers on --json) reporting lines-per-cue as libass will lay them out. Five of this iteration's six loose Look lines are agents describing a picture they had on disk but never measured.
Fix the rc1 fixture: give its project.json a captions stage so 'don't redo the captions' has something to cache, then re-run rc1 and rc2 together.

silence.py --filler: decide whether it should leave silences alone unless asked (fw1 and fw3 each removed ~5 s nobody requested, both disclosed). 1.18 decision; at minimum the SKILL.md row must say what the default does.
silence.py's --filler error text should name whisper.cpp / faster-whisper / openai-whisper and a pip line, so fw2-shaped refusals are actionable without the agent inventing engine names.

Eval 20: re-run this 18-id set plus the full 100 at 1.17.2, and grade the caption prompts on the sheet rather than on the fit stats - the question is how many lines the rendered frame has, not what the fitter reports.
